artboards.title: New tab — name and contacts optional
Trends — by tab, not by person
Option B — tabs as folder tiles

annotations.text:
THE MODEL
A tab is a folder. It holds costs and money back, and it has a name if you give it one.
Contacts are optional labels on a tab, picked from the phone book. There is no People list to keep and no Add person screen — the People and Settled sections on today’s Lending page go away.

WHAT COUNTS
Every cost on an open tab adds to Owed to you, whether or not anyone is named on it. Today a tab with nobody on it raises no claim, so it never reaches the total — that has to change underneath (a claim held by the tab itself).
No name typed? The tab takes its contacts’ names, or the first cost’s.

IPHONE
Safari has no contact picker. On an iPhone the Contacts button is not there, so typing a name stays the way in. A typed name is still only a label on the tab.

BILLS AND REMINDERS
Attaching is offered the moment a cost is saved, and any time after from the swipe. Remind uses the share sheet and carries the bill, as the person page already does. When nobody is named, Remind opens the share sheet with the message and no names.

SWIPE
The same SwipeRow as Budgets: commit off, so a long swipe never deletes. Delete undoes for 15 minutes. A tab row on the Loan centre swipes to Remind · Add cost.

OPTION B — FOLDER TILES
For: reads most like folders, and each tab gets more room.
Against: amounts no longer share one right edge, and past about six tabs you scroll a grid, and a tile cannot swipe, so Remind and Add cost move inside the tab. The list (Main) is the recommendation.
